public_payload.normalized_proposition: ChatGPT's bias guardrails are imperfect, both too strict and too loose, and can be circumvented.

statement.document_title: Large Language Models like ChatGPT say The Darnedest Things

from_speaker: The patch works to some extent
if you now run the prompt in figure 7
in some ways too strict and others too loose
get around these “guardrails” by framing the requests in various indirect ways
the guardrails often lead to outputs that are absurdly over-cautious
our_interpretation: The claim concerns ChatGPT after the bias-related patch described in the preceding sentences, as experienced by the January 9, 2023 post. Launch-era failures alone cannot settle it.
The ordinary reading is that indirect requests could still elicit discriminatory responses, while safeguards also repeatedly obstructed harmless requests through inappropriate refusals or cautions.

The target period begins with the unspecified patch and ends on the post date. Its start is left null because the source supplies no patch date. Evidence must independently establish that it concerns the patched state.

No numerical failure rate is specified. Documented examples can establish bypasses; repeated examples or systematic testing are needed to substantiate the contextual description of over-caution as recurring.
criteria.support_condition: Independent records of the relevant patched ChatGPT establish both successful indirect bypasses of bias safeguards and recurring inappropriate refusals or cautions on harmless requests before or at publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable testing of the relevant patched ChatGPT rebuts at least one component: the purported bypasses do not survive the patch, or the supposed over-cautious responses are justified or not a recurring behavior. Isolated successful safeguards do not contradict an assertion of imperfection.
